Join keys as index pairs

Source: R/grp-join.R
grp_join.Rd

grp_join() matches the rows of x and y on key columns and returns the index pairs, never a table. Pairs come in x's row order and, within a row of x, in y's. grp_match() is the first match of each row of x, as base::match() gives for one key, over one or several keys.

Usage

grp_join(x, y, by = NULL, type = "inner", multiple = "all")

grp_match(x, y)

Arguments

x, y

Key vectors (integer, double, logical, character, factor, integer64, or a list of raw vectors), or a data frame or list of them. A data frame uses all its columns, unless by names some.

by

NULL, to pair the key columns of x and y by position, or the names of the key columns, when x and y are data frames or named lists. A named element, as in c(customer = "id"), pairs x's customer with y's id.

type

"inner", "left" (every row of x, with NA in y when it has no match), "semi" (the rows of x with a match) or "anti" (those without).

multiple

When a row of x matches several rows of y: "all" pairs, the "first" or "last" match, or "error", a zutable_multiple_error naming the first such key.

Value

grp_join(): a list of x and y, integer row indices of one length; for "semi" and "anti", x alone. grp_match(): an integer vector as long as x, NA where there is no match.

Details

NA matches NA; for doubles NA and NaN are different keys and -0 matches 0. Strings match when their text does, whatever their encoding; a factor matches by its labels, against a factor or a character key. Integer, logical and double keys match by value. A character key against a number, or an integer64 key against anything but another, is a zutable_type_error.

Examples

grp_join(c("a", "b", "a"), c("b", "a", "a"))
#> $x
#> [1] 1 1 2 3 3
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 2 3 1 2 3
#> 
grp_join(c(1, 2, 3), c(3, 1), type = "left")
#> $x
#> [1] 1 2 3
#> 
#> $y
#> [1]  2 NA  1
#> 
grp_match(c("b", "z", "a"), c("a", "b", "b"))
#> [1]  2 NA  1
orders <- data.frame(customer = c(10L, 20L, 10L), day = 1:3)
people <- data.frame(id = c(10L, 20L), name = c("Ada", "Linus"))
grp_join(orders, people, by = c(customer = "id"))
#> $x
#> [1] 1 2 3
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 1 2 1
#>
